question.text: A Cat III manager expecting a market correction would MOST LIKELY position which strategy type?

explanation.text: The Logic: Short-bias maintains net-short exposure — benefits from downward moves. Dedicated-long bleeds in corrections. Pre-IPO and Activist are long-oriented. The Trap: Dedicated-Long, Pre-IPO, and Activist strategies all carry net-long posture and would suffer in a correction. Note: Short-bias is the directional strategy defined in Sections 10.1.1.4 / 10.1.1.5 as maintaining net short exposure that benefits from downward market movement.
